# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 77 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | Coptic

---

## Saying 77

Jesus said: "I am the light that is over all things. I am the all. From me the all came forth, and to me the all attained. Split a piece of wood; I am there. Lift up the stone, and you will find me there."

---

**Translator's Notes (EMET):**

- **ⲁⲛⲅ ⲡⲟⲩⲟⲉⲓⲛ ⲉⲧϩⲓϫⲛ ⲧⲏⲣϥ** / "I am the light over the all" — a cosmic claim of divine immanence
- **ⲡⲧⲏⲣϥ** / *ptērf*: "the all" — the totality; a Gnostic term for the pleroma/fullness
- "From me the all came forth" — the *ex me* creation claim; the light as source of all existence
- "To me the all attained" — return of the all to its source; the circular cosmology
- **ⲱϥⲧ ⲛⲟⲩϣⲉ ⲛϩⲱⲧ** / "split a piece of wood" — the pantheistic or panentheistic conclusion: Jesus present in the material world
- "Lift up the stone" — found me there: ubiquitous presence
- The wood/stone portion was found in POxy 1 (Greek) in a different position; Thomas places it here as the culmination of the "I am" saying
